clusters.name: Walter moving the family across the country, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move from Millbrook to Sorrel Valley in March 1952, within the year: June's homesickness and daily letters to her sister, her distance from Walter as he worked the orchard, Glen's fights at school, Walter's cutoff from his brother Harlan over their father's land money, June's weeks in bed that first winter, rows between Walter and June over money for trees, and by September June had joined the church choir and her letters thinned out. The shifts pile up across the first eighteen months in the valley, each touching another person as the family settled into a new place.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when the frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan: Walter drank heavily, he and Glen blamed each other, Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank, Carl's asthma attacks worsened, you began wetting the bed in April 1969, your grandmother Ida's heart trouble was found, and by October Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees. The shifts in functioning and relationship, and the symptoms in the children, gather around the months when the orchard was lost and the family moved to Ridgeport.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's job lost when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975: Glen sat in the truck for hours out of work, loud fights broke out between Glen and Marian over money at night, Marian took a second job cleaning offices, you stopped eating properly and lost weight, you kept to your room and grew distant from your mother, Walter drank again after six years off it, and by June 1976 you were eating and made the track team. Your mother's overfunctioning, the conflict between your parents, and your own symptom and distance from her moved together across these months as your father's functioning fell.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into Nora and Hollis's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma's move from her farm into your house in January 1990: you clashed with her over the children's bedtimes and meals, Hollis worked late and kept out of the rows, he took his mother's side, Owen had tantrums at preschool, Wilma took over Lily's care, you developed eczema on both hands, rows with Hollis filled most nights, and by June 1991 Wilma took a flat in town and your eczema cleared over the summer. The shifts in relationship—your conflict with Wilma, your distance from Hollis, his toward move toward his mother, and Wilma's overfunctioning with Lily—pile up across these eighteen months as the household adjusted to a third adult in it.
